data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Preferring the better-corroborated theory is defensible on Popper's terms as a non-inductive 'critical preference' grounded in verisimilitude (truth-likeness) and empirical content, not probability; this avoids smuggling in induction by treating preference as a rational guess toward truth rather than an expectation of future success, but accepting this costs the agent any guarantee of predictive reliability or practical safety, forcing action to remain a risky leap without probabilistic insurance.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the Tich\u00fd/Miller proof holds that verisimilitude cannot be consistently defined in rich languages, then the appeal to truth-likeness collapses into an empty metaphor.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'acting on' a theory inherently requires assigning it a higher subjective probability of success, then the distinction between corroboration and probability is merely semantic, and induction is smuggled back in via the backdoor of praxis.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Popper's own advice to prefer corroborated theories implies an expectation of future performance, then his system is performatively self-contradictory.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism distinguishes between 'justification for belief' (which Popper rejects) and 'preference for criticism' (which he accepts). A theory with higher empirical content has survived more severe tests, making it a better candidate for being close to the truth (verisimilitude), even if its logical probability remains low or undefined. Scientists prefer it not because they expect it to work (induction), but because it is the most informative and least refuted map available. The 'cost' is the explicit admission that this preference offers no pragmatic shield against failure; acting on the best-corroborated theory is still acting on a falsifiable conjecture, meaning bridges built on it may still collapse, and the scientist bears full responsibility for the risk without the comfort of inductive certainty.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
